text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Economic affairs ministry managed to attract almost two billion guilders in foreign investments to the Netherlands last years. (p1)
- Battle for control over Air Holdings enters second round as J&J Investments lodge an appeal with The Hague court. (p1)
- Collapse of planemaker Fokker seems to provide Dutch aerospace industry with an impulse for further development. (p1)
- Food company Nutricia rejects activists' criticism on how it is selling baby milk.(p3)
- National rail NS seeks alliance with regional bus company Veonn in province of Friesland. (p3)
- Amsterdam court rejects all claims against LCI Computer Groep of Den Bosch. (p3)
- Unions call for clarification on new round of restructuring at steelmaker Nedstaal. (p4)
- Market-maker AOT has closed its office in Cologne, Germany on January 1. (p9)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Social affairs minister Ad Melkert promises compensation for people on minimum wages to pay for heating during the fierce cold. (p1)
- Hutu opposition in Burundi angry about brewer Heineken's decision to extend its production in the country. (p2)
- ABN Amro bank to introduce new warrant on the Nifty Fifteen, 15 of the bank's favourite shares. (p13)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Suspects of burglary at state criminal investigation team LRT building in Zeist caught, but computers containing secret information still missing. (p1)
- Funeral insurance unit of insurer Levob taken over by insurer Aegon's subsidiary De Nederlandse Verzekeringsgroep. (p25)
- Engineering sector is not able to pay extra wage costs, according to employers' negotiator. (p25)
- Bourse-listed funds of insurer AXA Leven had a record year in 1996 with 45.1 pct return on investment. (p27)
TROUW
- French staff of Akzo Nobel to protest in The Hague on Saturday against the company's restructuring at its unit Riom.
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Strikes threaten at Postkantoren BV, a joint unit of ING and Dutch PTT (KPN). (p11)
